from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [

        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Concept of Directed Area", lecture_lines)
        
        # Mobjects for animations
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(square.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Intuition: The Right-Hand Rule", [
            "The right-hand rule determines direction.",
            "Order of input vectors matters.",
            "The cross product is normal to the plane."
        ])
        
        # Create visual components
        # Vectors: A, B, and Cross Product C
        vec_a = Vector(UP, color=WHITE)
        vec_b = Vector(RIGHT, color=WHITE)
        vec_c = Vector(OUT, color=WHITE)
        
        # Labels
        label_a = MathTex(r"\vec{a}").next_to(vec_a.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        label_b = MathTex(r"\vec{b}").next_to(vec_b.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        label_c = MathTex(r"\vec{a} \times \vec{b}").next_to(vec_c.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Group them
        vectors = VGroup(vec_a, vec_b, vec_c, label_a, label_b, label_c)
        self.place_at_grid(vectors, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(vec_a), Create(vec_b), Write(label_a), Write(label_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Flip vectors to show order matters
        self.play(
            vec_a.animate.rotate(PI, axis=RIGHT),
            label_a.animate.next_to(vec_a.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Create(vec_c), Write(label_c))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Scalar triple product calculates signed volume.",
            "Volume represents the 3D linear transformation.",
            "Parallelepiped volume is the determinant.",
            "Cross product is a 3D volume tool.",
            "Volume relates base area and height."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Linear Transformations & Change of Volume", lecture_lines)
        
        # Initial shapes
        cube = Cube(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2)
        prism = Prism(dimensions=[1.5, 2.0, 1.2], fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Scalar triple product calculates signed volume."
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(cube, 'B2')
        self.play(Create(cube))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Volume represents the 3D linear transformation."
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFA500")
        self.play(Transform(cube, prism))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Parallelepiped volume is the determinant."
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        det_text = Text("det(A)", font_size=30).set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(det_text, 'E4')
        self.play(Write(det_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Cross product is a 3D volume tool."
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(cube.animate.rotate(PI/4, axis=OUT), run_time=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Volume relates base area and height."
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        vol_text = Text("Volume = |det(A)|", font_size=30).set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(vol_text, 'F3')
        self.play(FadeIn(vol_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Physical World (Torque)", [
            "Torque is defined as r cross F.",
            "Cross product captures leverage effects.",
            "Perpendicular forces cause rotation."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        r_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color=WHITE)
        f_vec = Arrow(start=RIGHT*2, end=RIGHT*2 + UP*1.5, color=WHITE)
        torque_label = MathTex(r"\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}", color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(r_vec, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(f_vec, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(torque_label, 'A3')
        
        self.play(Create(r_vec), Create(f_vec), Write(torque_label))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        leverage_text = Text("Leverage = |r||F|sin(θ)", font_size=20, color="#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(leverage_text, 'E3')
        self.play(Write(leverage_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        rotation_arrow = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI/2, color="#00CED1")
        rotation_arrow.move_to(self.grid['C2'] + RIGHT*0.3 + UP*0.3)
        self.play(Create(rotation_arrow))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Cross product combines direction and area.",
            "It links geometry to linear operators.",
            "It scales volumes in linear transformations."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements to animate
        # 1. Geometric objects (Area/Normal)
        plane = Surface(lambda u, v: np.array([u, v, 0]), u_range=[-1, 1], v_range=[-1, 1], color=BLUE).set_opacity(0.3)
        normal = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=OUT*1.5, color=WHITE)
        geom = VGroup(plane, normal)
        self.place_in_area(geom, 'B2', 'C4', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # 2. Linear Operator/Scaling
        volume = Cube(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.4, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(volume, 'E3', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(geom))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(volume))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(volume.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF7F"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Geometric Magic of Cross Products: From Areas to Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Directed Area
sections.content: Briefly revisit the 2D determinant representing the signed area of a parallelogram. Introduce the leap to 3D by defining the cross product as a vector perpendicular to the plane formed by two input vectors, with a magnitude equal to the area of the parallelogram they span.
sections.example: Imagine a robotic arm moving two rods; the 'sweep' between them creates a flat shape whose orientation and size define our new vector.

sections.title: Geometric Intuition: The Right-Hand Rule
sections.content: Visualize the cross product as a physical orientation. Use the Right-Hand Rule to explain how the order of vectors (a × b vs b × a) flips the direction of the resulting vector, emphasizing its role as a 'normal' vector.
sections.example: Use a character, 'Agent Vector', pointing fingers to show how the thumb always points 'up' relative to the floor spanned by the index and middle fingers.

sections.title: Linear Transformations & Change of Volume
sections.content: Connect the cross product to the concept of the Scalar Triple Product. Explain how the cross product is not just a vector, but a tool to compute the signed volume of a parallelepiped, which represents the determinant of a 3D linear transformation.
sections.example: An animation of a 3D cube morphing into a slanted prism: the volume change is quantified by the interaction of the cross product of the base vectors with the third vector.

sections.title: Application: The Physical World (Torque)
sections.content: Apply the cross product to physics. Define Torque (τ = r × F). Show how the cross product captures the 'leverage' effect—where only the component of force perpendicular to the radius arm causes rotation.
sections.example: A squirrel trying to open a round nutcracker: the force applied at the tip (r) creates rotation based on the cross product with the force vector (F).

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Cross product = Direction (Normal) + Magnitude (Area). It serves as the fundamental bridge between geometric configuration and the volume-scaling nature of linear operators.
sections.example: A quick visual recap showing the transition from two lines on a screen to a 3D volume, linking the 'Area' concept back to the 'Linear Transformation' concept.
